messages:
nora_chan: Hi all, first-week quick question — I'm running the JS streaming SDK sample locally and after ~10s the client gets a 429. Should I be using the hosted org API key or a separate sandbox/dev key for local streaming tests?

 diego_r: welcome aboard! :tada: use the sandbox key for local experimentation. Hosted keys are for staging/prod and have different billing + quota buckets. sandbox streaming is intentionally conservative to prevent noisy dev workloads from impacting production.

nora_chan: thanks — where is the sandbox key in the Console? I only see a Hosted API Key under my profile.

clare: Console -> API Keys -> choose your org/team -> there should be a "Sandbox" tab. If its missing it might be because trial credits ran out or provisioning didn't finish; ping #eng-infra or open the internal form. Also watch the 429 body: it usually contains a rate_bucket string like "rate_bucket=sb_stream_lite" which helps infra triage.

infra-bot: Reminder: When filing infra tickets about 429s include the entire response JSON, the rate_bucket id, and your request patterns. Quota increase link: https://intranet.redwood/company-forms/compute-quota

ben: a couple of quick tips from infra: 1) shorten demo prompts while iterating, 2) disable tight retry loops in dev, 3) implement exponential backoff reading the Retry-After header, and 4) if you need higher dev streaming throughput request a temporary dev bump via the quota form and mention "new hire dev streaming".

nora_chan: perfect, i'll check the Sandbox tab and file the quota request if needed. i'll paste the 429 response and rate_bucket here if it persists. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
